meta.description: Integrate multimodal single-cell data (CITE-seq RNA+protein, 10x Multiome RNA+ATAC, unpaired/diagonal RNA+ATAC) and choose the right joint method. Use when classifying an integration task by anchor structure (paired vs unpaired), denoising CITE-seq ADT background before joint embedding, picking between WNN, totalVI, MultiVI, MOFA+, GLUE, or Seurat v5 bridge integration, or diagnosing why a modality dominates a joint clustering.

scientific_integrity.detail: All 12 cited references (Argelaguet 2021, Stoeckius 2017, Mule 2022 DSB, Hao 2021 WNN, Gayoso 2021 totalVI, Ashuach 2023 MultiVI, Argelaguet 2020 MOFA+, Cao & Gao 2022 GLUE, Hao 2024 bridge, Bredikhin 2022 MUON, Ghazanfar 2024 StabMap, Yin 2024 DecontPro) are real, correctly attributed papers. No fabricated statistics, p-values, or results appear anywhere in the 7 outputs; all numeric results in executed outputs came from real code runs on labeled synthetic data.

practice_boundaries.detail: Input 7 explicitly asked for an individual patient's lupus risk from immune proportions; the correct response declines this as out of scope for a computational-methods skill and confines the answer to the mosaic-integration method question. No diagnostic or prescriptive language appears anywhere else in the skill.

methodological_ground.detail: The skill repeatedly and correctly flags model-dependent inference as such (imputed modalities are not measurements, ATAC gene-activity is not RNA, RNA/protein discordance is often real biology and should not be 'corrected away'), which is the opposite of a methodological fallacy -- this is above-average rigor for the genre.

code_usability.detail: All code the skill itself ships (CITE-seq DSB+WNN in R, totalVI in Python, Multiome TF-IDF/LSI+WNN in R) ran unmodified in Inputs 1, 2 and 4 with no syntax errors or missing dependencies. The one execution failure (Input 5, MultiVI mosaic) used code the skill does not provide at all -- there is nothing shipped to judge as unrunnable there; it is recorded as a completeness gap (P1), not a code-usability failure.

functional_suitability.note: WNN/DSB, totalVI and Multiome-WNN each get a full worked code block and all three ran unmodified; MultiVI, StabMap, Cobolt and Seurat v5 bridge integration are named as primary methods for 2 of the 4 classified anchor structures (mosaic, unpaired-via-bridge) but ship zero code.

reliability.note: Category-3 override applied (hard stops are correct design, strict rejection is not penalized). Common Errors table documents 8 real failure modes accurately, but the DSB code block itself has no runtime guard against its own documented 'no empty droplets' failure -- verified it fails silently with no warning.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md is 249 lines with a separate usage-guide.md and examples/; well within budget, no bloat.

agent_usability.note: Decision tables and per-method 'Use when / Fails when' framing are unusually clear and consistent; minor deduction because several code blocks assume an already-constructed 'obj'/'mdata' rather than a runnable standalone script.

human_usability.note: Category-3 override applied to Forgiveness. Natural example prompts in usage-guide.md trigger correctly; the Governing Principle (classify anchor structure first) is itself the mechanism that handles ambiguous/off-spec requests, verified in Input 7.

security.note: No secrets, no eval/exec of raw strings, no prompt-injection vectors. File paths are passed to Read10X/mu.read_10x_h5 without validation, typical and low-risk for this genre.

maintainability.note: examples/ only covers 1 of 6 documented methods (CITE-seq WNN, one file per language); the other 5 methods live only as inline SKILL.md snippets, and the totalVI path is not reproducible across runs as shipped (verified, see dynamic_score input 2).

agent_specific.note: Trigger description and Related Skills boundaries are precise. Idempotency is verified solid for the WNN/DSB path (identical clusters across 2 runs) but verified NOT solid for totalVI (max abs latent diff 0.9723 across 2 unseeded runs on identical input), with no warning given to the agent about this.

key_strengths: The Governing Principle (classify anchor structure first) is unusually rigorous and correctly redirected an ambiguous, adversarially-framed request (Input 7) to the right method class without being told to.

The Common Errors table is accurate, not aspirational: 2 of its 8 documented failure modes were independently reproduced exactly as described (DSB without true empty droplets silently produces nonsense; ATAC LSI_1 tracks depth).

Every method the skill actually ships code for -- CITE-seq DSB+WNN (R), totalVI (Python), Multiome TF-IDF/LSI+WNN (R) -- ran unmodified and correctly recovered ground-truth cell populations on synthetic data (100%, and ~91% concordance respectively).

Methodological-rigor warnings (imputed values are not measurements, ATAC gene-activity is not RNA, RNA/protein discordance is often real biology and should not be 'corrected away') go beyond what most bioinformatics skills document.

recommendations.title: totalVI pattern is undocumented as non-deterministic
recommendations.problem: The documented totalVI pattern does not set scvi.settings.seed. Two runs of the exact SKILL.md code on identical input produced latent representations differing by up to 0.9723 (max abs); setting the seed makes reruns bit-identical.
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md's totalVI code block was written without a reproducibility step, unlike the R/Seurat paths which inherit Seurat's default seed.use=42.
recommendations.fix: Add `scvi.settings.seed = 0` (or similar) as the first line of the totalVI code block, and add a one-line note that scvi-tools VAE training is stochastic unless seeded. Apply the same fix to the GLUE pattern, which has the identical gap.

recommendations.title: Mosaic anchor structure (MultiVI/StabMap/Cobolt) ships zero runnable code
recommendations.problem: Mosaic is one of the 4 anchor structures the skill's own Governing Principle classifies tasks into, and MultiVI/StabMap/Cobolt are named as its methods, but none of the three has a code block anywhere in SKILL.md, usage-guide.md, or examples/ -- unlike WNN, totalVI, Multiome-WNN and GLUE, which all get one.
recommendations.root_cause: The skill's worked examples cover the two paired assays (CITE-seq, Multiome) and one unpaired method (GLUE) but the mosaic branch was left as a decision-table entry only.
recommendations.fix: Add at least one worked MultiVI example (scvi.data.organize_multiome_anndatas + scvi.model.MULTIVI.setup_anndata + train), mirroring the totalVI block's structure. Note for the fixer: organize_multiome_anndatas in scvi-tools 1.5.1 currently errors against anndata>=0.11 (AttributeError: 'AnnData' object has no attribute 'concatenate') -- verify against the pinned anndata version or provide a manual-concatenation fallback.

recommendations.title: DSB's own documented failure mode has no runtime guard
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's Common Errors table correctly warns that passing a filtered-only matrix as empty_drop_matrix produces 'nonsense output', but the DSB code block itself performs no check and DSBNormalizeProtein raises no error or warning when this happens -- confirmed it runs silently to completion with a visibly different, invalid output range.
recommendations.root_cause: The failure mode is documented in prose but not defended against in the shipped code pattern.
recommendations.fix: Add a minimal sanity check before calling DSBNormalizeProtein, e.g. compare median total ADT counts between cell_protein_matrix and empty_drop_matrix and warn/stop if they are not clearly lower in the empty matrix.

recommendations.title: Bundled CITE-seq examples skip the skill's own DSB-before-WNN recommendation
recommendations.problem: examples/cite_seq_analysis.R and examples/cite_seq_analysis.py both normalize ADT with CLR only and never read a raw/unfiltered matrix, even though SKILL.md's body states raw or CLR-only ADT 'carries this background into the joint graph' and instructs denoising with DSB (or totalVI) before any joint embedding.
recommendations.root_cause: The examples/ files appear to have been written as a simpler CLR-only quickstart before the DSB-first guidance was added to the SKILL.md body, and were not updated to match.
recommendations.fix: Either update both example files to call DSB (R) / note that Python has no first-party DSB equivalent and recommend totalVI instead, or add an explicit comment in both files noting they are a fallback path and pointing to the DSB block in SKILL.md.

recommendations.title: Seurat v5 bridge integration is named but never demonstrated
recommendations.problem: PrepareBridgeReference() is named in the skill's opening summary line and in the method decision table as a primary unpaired/diagonal method, but unlike GLUE it never gets a worked code example.
recommendations.root_cause: Same pattern as the mosaic gap: the decision table is ahead of the worked examples.
recommendations.fix: Add a short worked bridge-integration example (reference multiome dataset, PrepareBridgeReference, MapQuery) alongside the GLUE block.
